# Frozen scalar compatibility baseline

These are fictional test inputs, not provider output or user data. Production
behavior and the existing public `tests/fixtures/product_scope/mod.rs` were pinned
to GitManager commit `c527ef892ddec9af6ed37431898133ce36054c62` when captured.
The reused fixture source SHA-256 is
`05443731d1b627cc4d9e1389ba52c17a88a182a196a48665b1403962b9ecf469`.

Each `.gmbak` is **literal canonical JSON emitted by that implementation**. A
capsule carries the complete old snapshot, its exact intention bundle, and the
original extension byte arrays. Keeping these together avoids redundant copies
of the same snapshot and extensions. No expected snapshot is generated by the
current serializer during the normal tests.

The six capsules cover:

- `active`: a future-work scalar layer, an independently recorded ordinary
  promised-date obligation, reachable scene/mapping packages, historical seed
  correspondences, later completed work, protected metadata, events and export
- `evolved`: same-layer implementation evolution, retaining those business facts
- `withdrawn`: that layer withdrawn on current data, retaining facts, all scalar
  proofs, original source provenance and the independent active obligation
- `paired`: a separate minimal single-layer lineage with two retained evolution
  rehearsals and one pending Deferred decision, without activating either option
- `prospective`: initial first-layer BothNeeded recording, pending and replayable,
  with no committed layer or live metadata initialization
- `legacy-v1`: an actual frozen format-1 snapshot and backup with its ordinary
  decision/packages; produced once by the established format-1 fixture method,
  then retained literally rather than deriving it from a future serializer

`manifest.json` freezes file SHA-256 and length, canonical snapshot SHA-256 and
Data-domain identity, every nested snapshot/package digest at its JSON pointer,
raw captured-source checksums and producer/artifact identities, each scalar proof
payload checksum, existing layer/composition/initialization/correspondence
identities, bundle identity/checksum, backup payload identity and checkpoint
filename. `scope_payloads` additionally hashes complete registry payloads in the
existing Adoption domain; these are test inventory checksums, not new runtime
proof authority. The test pins the manifest's SHA-256 independently of the
reproduction helper. `SHA256SUMS` provides a plain external checksum inventory.

Version dependencies deliberately remain separate:

- Generated-project container: 2 (legacy input: 1)
- Scalar state, layer, manifest and rehearsal compiler: 1
- Archive object, intention bundle and backup envelope: 1
- Runtime: `local-interpreter/4`; semantic driver: `semantic-input/3`
- Canonical domain prefix: `gitmanager.product.v1` followed by NUL
- Compiled source provenance: exact `Verified host scope composition v1: ...`

Normal tests validate literal byte identity, deterministic scalar recompilation,
all retained package bindings, fresh replay, verified reopen/recovery, unchanged
checkpoint discovery and explicit format-1 upgrade. Rehashed proof tampering,
missing packages and corrupt package bytes must be rejected. Future migration
work must preserve these files and values; adapt the entry-point assertions to
explicit upgrade semantics instead of regenerating the baseline.

## Reproduction (never a routine update command)

The ignored `reproduce_scalar_baseline` test uses public synthetic fixtures and
production APIs only. On the pinned pre-migration implementation, with this
**test-only** helper applied, run:

```sh
SCALAR_FIXTURE_OUTPUT=/absolute/new/output \
  cargo test --locked --test product_scope_compatibility_test \
  reproduce_scalar_baseline -- --exact --ignored
```

The output directory must not exist. The helper never overwrites the committed
fixtures. Compare the resulting files with this baseline; do not replace hashes
when a newer serializer differs. Construction uses fixed IDs, dates and random
seeds, temporary local stores and bounded histories; no clocks, network, provider
or private acceptance input participates. Tests bound each capsule to 4 MiB and
the complete six-capsule corpus to 8 MiB. The files are text JSON, not executables
or a packaged build.
